Rome Odunze's 2025 ended with a foot injury, Out from week 14 on, and he played just 12 of 17. That's the one real knock on him, because the job in front of him is as good as it gets at his ADP. He was on the field for 88% of Chicago's snaps, WR10 among qualifying receivers, and pulled 23.7% of the targets. He also gets a full second year of Ben Johnson calling the plays, which matters more for a 24-year-old first-rounder than anything on the depth chart.
Round 5 value among the 448 on our board

The production hasn't caught the usage yet, and our projection docks him for it. His 12.2 points a game last year costs him 1.2 a game, and a 24.6% touchdown share drags him down a touch more. The red-zone work was thin too, just 5 touches inside the ten and a 13.3% share of his own touches there. That's the gap: if Johnson starts manufacturing scoring looks for him, the jump from 146 points to our 199 happens fast. If he doesn't, you're drafting a high-volume receiver who settles for yards.
We have him at pick 50, so drafters take him 4.8 picks later. ADP 54.8 from PPR drafts, Sep 5 to Sep 9.

We put him at 199 points, about 14 over the average season for receivers taken around pick 55, and he sits at WR26 on our board, rank 50 overall. Drafters have drifted past him since early September, down nearly three picks. We'd take him a round before that instead. The foot keeps him from being a top-20 lock, but at WR26 he's the upside pick in that range.
